# Assembly Constraints++ for Alibre Design

- Assembly Constraints++ is a starter add-on that gives you a complete working shell to replace with your own tooling, and the constraint features the name promises are not written yet.
  - What it does today
    - Registers its own ribbon menu with one command, so you can see an add-on load and run.
    - Hosts a Python runtime and runs a bundled script when the command fires.
    - Ships a sample command that generates internal or external involute spur gear sketches on a plane you pick.
    - Binds the active part or assembly before the script runs.
    - Includes the manifest, a registry template, and an installer template for packaging.
  - What you need
    - Alibre Design with the AlibreScript add-on installed.
    - The .NET Framework 4.8.1 runtime on 64-bit Windows.
    - Visual Studio or MSBuild if you want to build it yourself.
  - Getting started
    - Clone the repository and run `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
    - Build the solution in `source/` in Release configuration.
    - Copy the build output into your Alibre Design add-ons directory.
    - Start Alibre Design and run the command to confirm the shell works, then replace the sample script with your own.
  - Where things live
    - `source/` holds the VB.NET add-on, the sample script, and the packaging assets.
    - `documentation/` holds reference notes.
    - `reviews/` holds dated code reviews.
  - Good to know
    - The gear generator is there to prove the pipeline runs end to end, not because the add-on is about gears.
  - Use it under the MIT License.
